source.author: verg
source.text: Tu potes unanimos armare in proelia fratres atque odiis versare domos, tu verbera tectis funereasque inferre faces, tibi nomina mille, mille nocendi artes.
source.text_original: Tu potes unanimos armare in proelia fratres / atque odiis versare domos, tu verbera tectis / funereasque inferre faces, tibi nomina mille, / mille nocendi artes.
source.text_english: You are able to arm brothers of one mind for battle and turn homes into hatred; you bring whips into houses and funeral torches; you have a thousand names, a thousand arts of doing harm.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: inde me persequitur luxuria, inde auaritia conatur irrumpere, inde uenter meus uult mihi deus esse pro Christo, compellit libido, ut habitantem in me spiritum sanctum fugem, ut templum eius uiolem, persequitur me, inquam , hostis, cui nomina mille, mille nocendi artes: et ego infelix uictorem me putabo, dum capior?
reuse.text_original: inde me persequitur luxuria, inde auaritia conatur irrumpere, inde uenter meus uult mihi deus esse pro Christo, compellit libido, ut habitantem in me spiritum sanctum fugem, ut templum eius uiolem, persequitur me, inquam , hostis, cui nomina mille, mille nocendi artes: et ego infelix uictorem me putabo, dum capior?
reuse.text_english: From there luxury keeps pursuing me, from there avarice tries to break in, from there my belly wants to be a god to me instead of Christ, lust urges me to flee the Holy Spirit dwelling in me, to violate his temple. The enemy, I say, pursues me, with a thousand names and a thousand arts of doing harm; and shall I, unhappy man, think myself the victor while I am being captured?
